title: Bruce and the Spider
passage:
Hundreds of years ago, Robert Bruce was King of Scotland. He cared greatly for his land and people. The King of England desired control of Scotland and led a great army there. He tried to drive Bruce out. They fought six battles, and each time Bruce's army lost. After the last battle, his soldiers ran away, and Bruce sought out a cave to hide in. Bruce was ready to give up.

Then he saw a spider trying to make a web across the roof of the cave. It tried and failed six times. Bruce watched the spider and said, "Poor thing, you and I are alike." However, the spider didn't quit, and finally it succeeded. That gave Bruce a sense of hope. "I will try a seventh time too," he said.

Bruce gathered his soldiers and told them his plan. They spread the word, and soon Bruce had another army ready. This time, they beat their enemy and pushed them back to their own country. To this day, no one called Bruce will hurt a spider.
